## Model I

```{r mod1}
# 21) Core regressions
# --- Model 1: LN_SPPSF with time splines (SPSS runs this to get time coefficients)
formula_time <- ln_sppsf ~ arterial +
  single_family1story + half_duplex1story + half_duplex2story +
  smallest + small + large + largest +
  two_plus_baths + powder_room +
  good + fair + poor + very_poor_unsound +
  qabove_avg + qbelow_avg +
  yb_pre_1929 + yb_1946_to_1960 + yb_post_1961 +
  crawl + slab +
  ln_garagespaces + fireplace +
  hot_water + elec_baseboard + wall + central_air +
  months_1to9 + months_10to16 + months_17to24

mod_time <- backward_p(formula_time, data = df, p_out = 0.10, verbose = TRUE)
#summary(mod_time)

# --- Automatically pull time coefficients to compute RATEs (optional)
time_coefs <- coef(mod_time)[c("months_1to9", "months_10to16", "months_17to24")]
#time_coefs

# SPSS manually copies these: # rate1=-0.009842; rate2=0.022764; rate3=0
# If you'd rather hard-code like SPSS, set these explicitly.
rate1 <- unname(ifelse(is.na(time_coefs["months_1to9"]), 0, time_coefs["months_1to9"]))
rate2 <- unname(ifelse(is.na(time_coefs["months_10to16"]), 0, time_coefs["months_10to16"]))
rate3 <- unname(ifelse(is.na(time_coefs["months_17to24"]), 0, time_coefs["months_17to24"]))

# PRICE_INDEX and TAF (time adjustment factor)
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    price_index = (1 + rate1) ^ months_1to9 * (1 + rate2) ^ months_10to16 *
                  (1 + rate3) ^ months_17to24
  )

# Choose end_index = price_index at target month (SPSS: "last month")
# Here: by default, use the max MONTHS observed.
end_month <- max(df$months, na.rm = TRUE)
end_index <- df %>%  filter(months == end_month) %>%
  summarise(end_index = mean(price_index, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%  pull(end_index)

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    taf   = end_index / price_index,    tasp  = saleprice * taf,
    tasppsf = tasp / sresb_floorarea,   ln_tasp = log(tasp)
  )
```

```{r mod1a}
# 18. Diagnostics & ggplot charts for LN_SPPSF model
# 1) Get the rows that were actually used by the model
mf      <- model.frame(mod_time)          # model frame
row_idx <- as.integer(rownames(mf))           # row numbers in df

# 2) Subset df to those rows and augment
aug_sppsf <- augment(mod_time, data = df[row_idx, ]) |>
  mutate(    # back-transform from log if LN_SPPSF = log(SPPSF)
    PRED_SPPSF = exp(.fitted),    STD_RESID  = .std.resid
  )

# 3) Histogram of standardized residuals + normal curve
stats_resid <- aug_sppsf |>
  summarise(
    MEAN = mean(STD_RESID, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD   = sd(STD_RESID,   na.rm = TRUE),
    N    = sum(!is.na(STD_RESID))
  )

mu <- stats_resid$MEAN
sd_ <- stats_resid$SD
n_  <- stats_resid$N
binwidth <- 0.25

ggplot(aug_sppsf, aes(x = STD_RESID)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = binwidth, color = "black", fill = "steelblue") +
  stat_function(
    fun = function(x) dnorm(x, mean = mu, sd = sd_) * n_ * binwidth,    size = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Histogram\nDependent Variable: LN_SPPSF",
    x = "Regression Standardized Residual",    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",    x = Inf, y = Inf,    hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.5,
    label = sprintf("Mean = %.3f\nStd. Dev. = %.3f\nN = %d", mu, sd_, n_)
  ) +  theme_minimal()
```

```{r mod1c, results='asis'}
model_metrics_A(mod_time, "LN\\_SPPSF model fit statistics")
coef_table(mod_time, "LN\\_SPPSF model coefficients (95% CI)")
```

```{r mod1p}

ggplot(aug_sppsf, aes(x = months, y = STD_RESID)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, color = "red") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(10, 20), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Residuals for LN_SPPSF Model", x = "Months", y = "Standardized Residual") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r mod2}

  single_family1story + half_duplex1story + half_duplex2story +
  smallest + small + large + largest +
  two_plus_baths + powder_room +
  good + fair + poor + very_poor_unsound +
  qabove_avg + qbelow_avg +
  yb_pre_1929 + yb_1946_to_1960 + yb_post_1961 +
```

```{r mod2r}
# ---- INPUT ----
rows_used <- as.integer(rownames(model.frame(mod_ln_price_no_ecf)))  # which rows lm actually used
lev_vals  <- hatvalues(mod_ln_price_no_ecf)                          # length = nobs(mod)

lev_df <- df %>%  mutate(lev = NA_real_) %>%  mutate(lev = replace(lev, rows_used, lev_vals))

#lev_df <- df %>%
#  mutate(lev = hatvalues(mod_ln_price_no_ecf)) %>%   # mod is your lm object
#  transmute(lev) %>% #  filter(is.finite(lev))

# ---- STATS FOR ANNOTATION ----
mu <- mean(lev_df$lev)
sdv <- sd(lev_df$lev)
n  <- nrow(lev_df)

# ---- HIST BINNING (pick something SPSS-like) ----
# SPSS often picks a moderate number of bins; 25–35 works well here.
bins_n <- 30

# We need binwidth to scale the normal curve to "Frequency"
# density * N * binwidth ≈ counts
binwidth <- diff(range(lev_df$lev)) / bins_n

# label like SPSS (N = 2,286)
n_lab <- format(n, big.mark = ",")

ggplot(lev_df, aes(x = lev)) +  # histogram (Frequency)
  geom_histogram(
    bins = bins_n,    boundary = 0,    closed = "left",    fill = "deepskyblue2",
    color = "black",    linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  # Normal curve overlay, scaled to frequency
  stat_function(
    fun = function(x) dnorm(x, mean = mu, sd = sdv) * n * binwidth,    color = "black",
    linewidth = 1.3
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Histogram",    subtitle = "Dependent Variable: LN_PRICE",
    x = "Regression Leverage",    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  # annotation top-right
  annotate(
    "text",    x = Inf, y = Inf,    hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.2,
    label = paste0(
      "Mean = ", sprintf("%.2f", mu), "\n",
      "Std. Dev. = ", sprintf("%.3f", sdv), "\n",
      "N = ", n_lab
    ),    size = 4
  ) +
  # SPSS-ish styling: classic axes + horizontal grid lines
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", margin = margin(t = 10)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", margin = margin(r = 10)),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.6),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank()
  )
```

## Model III

```{r mod3}
# --- Model 3: BASE MODEL with ECFs (SPSS "BASE MODEL", dependent LN_PRICE)
# build RHS terms as character vector, then turn into a formula
rhs <- c(
  "ln_landratio", "ln_base_bldgsize_ratio",
  "arterial",
  "single_family1story", "half_duplex1story", "half_duplex2story",
  "smallest", "small", "large", "largest",
  "two_plus_baths", "powder_room",
  "good", "fair", "poor", "very_poor_unsound",
  "qabove_avg", "qbelow_avg",
  "yb_pre_1929", "yb_1946_to_1960", "yb_post_1961",
  "crawl", "slab",
  "ln_garagespaces", "fireplace",
  "hot_water", "elec_baseboard", "wall", "central_air",
  ecfs_col,  # <-- splices *all* secf_ dummy columns in correctly
  "months_1to9", "months_10to16", "months_17to24"
)

formula_base <- reformulate(rhs, response = "ln_price")

mod_base <- backward_p(formula_base, data = df, p_out = 0.10, verbose = TRUE)
summary(mod_base)

# Save predictions and influence measures similar to SPSS /SAVE=
df <- df %>%
  mutate(pre_1 = predict(mod_base, newdata = df), esp1  = exp(pre_1), ratio1 = esp1 / saleprice)

# Assessing metrics output
rrmetrics <- ratio_metrics(df, esp1, saleprice)

knitr::kable(
  rrmetrics,  format   = "latex",  booktabs = TRUE,
  caption  = "LN\\_PRICE model (base) assessing coefficients"   # <-- no \\_
  # escape = TRUE is the default; keep it that way
) %>%  kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position", "striped"), font_size = 8)

# Ratio stats like SPSS RATIO STATS ... BY ...
ratio_ecf   <- ratio_by(df, esp1, saleprice, ecf)
ratio_style <- ratio_by(df, esp1, saleprice, sresb_style)
ratio_cond  <- ratio_by(df, esp1, saleprice, scond)
ratio_size  <- ratio_by(df, esp1, saleprice, size)
ratio_era   <- ratio_by(df, esp1, saleprice, erabuilt)
ratio_fire  <- ratio_by(df, esp1, saleprice, fireplace)
ratio_priceclass <- ratio_by(df, esp1, saleprice, priceclass)

# Within bands (10/20/50)
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    within10_1 = if_else(ratio1 >= 0.9 & ratio1 <= 1.1, 1L, 0L),
    within20_1 = if_else(ratio1 >= 0.8 & ratio1 <= 1.2, 1L, 0L),
    within50_1 = if_else(ratio1 >= 0.5 & ratio1 <= 1.5, 1L, 0L)
  )

# 22) Outlier / influence removal (SPSS: COOK > 4/N, |SDRESID| > 2)
N_total <- nrow(df)
infl <- influence.measures(mod_base)
cook <- cooks.distance(mod_base)
stud <- rstudent(mod_base)

rows_used <- as.integer(rownames(model.frame(mod_base)))  # row numbers from the data used in lm()

df <- df %>%
  mutate(cook_1 = NA_real_,    stud_1  = NA_real_) |> 
  mutate(
    cook_1 = replace(cook_1, rows_used, cook),    stud_1 = replace(stud_1, rows_used, stud),
    in_inlier = if_else(cook_1 <= (4 / N_total) & abs(stud_1) <= 2, 1L, 0L)
    )

df_in <- df %>% filter(in_inlier == 1)

mod_base_inliers <- backward_p(formula_base, data = df_in, p_out = 0.10, verbose = TRUE)
#summary(mod_base_inliers)

df_in <- df_in %>%
  mutate(
    pre_2 = predict(mod_base_inliers, newdata = df_in),
    esp2  = exp(pre_2),    ratio2 = esp2 / saleprice,
    within10_2 = if_else(ratio2 >= 0.9 & ratio2 <= 1.1, 1L, 0L),
    within20_2 = if_else(ratio2 >= 0.8 & ratio2 <= 1.2, 1L, 0L),
    within50_2 = if_else(ratio2 >= 0.5 & ratio2 <= 1.5, 1L, 0L)
  )

# 23) Recalibrate time adjustments (SPSS shows an example with new RATEs)
# You can either:
#  - re-extract from a model that still has time splines, or  - set them manually.
# Here we demonstrate manual override:

time_coefs2 <- coef(mod_base)[c("months_1to9", "months_10to16", "months_17to24")]
#time_coefs2

# SPSS manually copies these:
# RATE1=-0.009842; RATE2=0.022764; RATE3=0
# If you'd rather hard-code like SPSS, set these explicitly.
RATE1_re <- unname(ifelse(is.na(time_coefs2["months_1to9"]), 0, time_coefs2["months_1to9"]))
RATE2_re <- unname(ifelse(is.na(time_coefs2["months_10to16"]), 0, time_coefs2["months_10to16"]))
RATE3_re <- unname(ifelse(is.na(time_coefs2["months_17to24"]), 0, time_coefs2["months_17to24"]))

df_in <- df_in %>%
  mutate(
    price_index_re = (1 + RATE1_re) ^ months_1to9 * (1 + RATE2_re) ^ months_10to16 *
                     (1 + RATE3_re) ^ months_17to24
  )

end_month_in <- max(df_in$months, na.rm = TRUE)
END_INDEX_re <- df_in %>%
  filter(months == end_month_in) %>%
  summarise(end_index = mean(price_index_re, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%  pull(end_index)

df_in <- df_in %>%
  mutate(
    taf_re  = END_INDEX_re / price_index_re,
    tasp_re = saleprice * taf_re,    ln_tasp_re = log(tasp_re)
  )

df_in1 <- df_in %>% select(saleid, pre_2, esp2, ratio2, within10_2, within20_2, within50_2,
                             price_index_re, taf_re, tasp_re, ln_tasp_re)

dfa <- df %>% left_join(df_in1, by = "saleid")
```

```{r mod3re}
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = label_number(accuracy = 0.01, big.mark = "", decimal.mark = ".")
    # If you want commas instead, use: label_number(big.mark = ",", accuracy = 1)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, NA),                      # keep y >= 0 like the SPSS plot
    breaks = seq(0, 5, 1),    labels = function(x) ifelse(x == 0, ".00", sprintf("%.2f", x))
  ) +
  labs(x = "ESP1", y = "RATIO1") +  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    # horizontal gridlines only, SPSS-like
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.6),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    # bold axis titles
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", margin = margin(t = 10)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", margin = margin(r = 10)),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    # keep axes lines prominent
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.8)
  )
```

## Model IV

```{r mod4}
# 24) Model with recalibrated time adjustments (dependent LN_TASP, remove time vars)
# SPSS: LN_TASP with ECFs, no months splines
rhs2 <- c(
  "ln_landratio", "ln_base_bldgsize_ratio",
  "arterial",
  "single_family1story", "half_duplex1story", "half_duplex2story",
  "smallest", "small", "large", "largest",
  "two_plus_baths", "powder_room",
  "good", "fair", "poor", "very_poor_unsound",
  "qabove_avg", "qbelow_avg",
  "yb_pre_1929", "yb_1946_to_1960", "yb_post_1961",
  "crawl", "slab",
  "ln_garagespaces", "fireplace",
  "hot_water", "elec_baseboard", "wall", "central_air",
  ecfs_col
)

formula_ln_tasp <- reformulate(rhs2, response = "ln_tasp_re")

mod_tasp <- backward_p(formula_ln_tasp, data = df_in, p_out = 0.10, verbose = TRUE)
#summary(mod_tasp)

df_in <- df_in %>%
  mutate(
    pre_3 = predict(mod_tasp, newdata = df_in), esp3  = exp(pre_3), ratio3 = esp3 / tasp_re
  )

rrmetrics <- ratio_metrics(df_in, esp3, saleprice)

knitr::kable(
  rrmetrics,  format   = "latex",  booktabs = TRUE,
  caption  = "LN\\_TASP model assessing coefficients" 
) %>%  kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position", "striped"), font_size = 8)

# 25) Alternative model (SPSS: LN_TASP with LN_LANDRATIO + LNSBLDSFINT + GARAGE + FIREPLACE, etc.)
rhs_alt <- c(
  "ln_landratio", "lnsbldsfint",
  "arterial",
  "single_family1story", "half_duplex1story", "half_duplex2story",
  "smallest", "small", "large", "largest",
  "two_plus_baths", "powder_room",
  "good", "fair", "poor", "very_poor_unsound",
  "qabove_avg", "qbelow_avg",
  "yb_pre_1929", "yb_1946_to_1960", "yb_post_1961",
  "crawl", "slab",
  "garage", "fireplace",
  "hot_water", "elec_baseboard", "wall", "central_air",
  ecfs_col
)

formula_alt <- reformulate(rhs_alt, response = "ln_tasp_re")

mod_alt <- backward_p(formula_alt, data = df_in, p_out = 0.10, verbose = TRUE)
#summary(mod_alt)

df_in <- df_in %>%
  mutate(
    pre_4 = predict(mod_alt, newdata = df_in), esp4  = exp(pre_4), ratio4 = esp4 / tasp_re
  )

rrmetrics <- ratio_metrics(df_in, esp4, saleprice)

knitr::kable(
  rrmetrics,  format   = "latex",  booktabs = TRUE,
  caption  = "Alternative LN\\_TASP model assessing coefficients" 
) %>%  kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position", "striped"), font_size = 8)

df_in2 <- df_in %>% select(saleid, pre_3, esp3, ratio3, pre_4, esp4, ratio4)

dfa <- dfa %>% left_join(df_in2, by = "saleid")
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
diagnose_predict_na <- function(model, newdata) {
  Terms <- delete.response(terms(model))

  mf <- model.frame(
    Terms,
    data = newdata,
    xlev = model$xlevels,
    na.action = na.pass
  )

  bad <- vapply(mf, function(x) any(is.na(x) | is.nan(x) | is.infinite(x)), logical(1))
  bad_vars <- names(bad)[bad]

  list(
    bad_vars = bad_vars,
    bad_values = mf[ , bad_vars, drop = FALSE],
    model_vars = names(mf)
  )
}

diag <- diagnose_predict_na(mod_base, nd)
diag$bad_vars
diag$bad_values

```
